newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-STAND-IN HYAM BAGS FIVE CATCHES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STAND-IN HYAM BAGS FIVE CATCHES.

text.p: Barry Hyam stood in as Essex wicketkeeper when Robert Rollins was ruled unfit and promptly equalled a club record in the Sunday League defeat of Middlesex at Chelmsford.
Hyam, 21, held five catches to equal the most taken by an Essex wicketkeeper in a limited overs match.
After reaching 256 in their 40 overs, Essex bowled out Middlesex for 190, Ashley Cowan taking four for 31.
Yorkshire, with Darren Gough, Richard Stemp and Craig White each taking three wickets, crushed Hampshire by 71 runs at Southampton.
Hampshire, chasing a modest 227-run target, lost their last nine wickets for 23 in just seven overs to lose by 71 runs.
Adam Hollioake's five-wicket haul for Surrey was not enough to save his side from a 12-run defeat by Kent at Canterbury.
Kent set the visiting side 193 but Dean Headley's four for 27 helped restrict Surrey to 181 for eight.

Lancashire avenged last week's Benson and Hedges Cup defeat by Derbyshire after Graham Lloyd, with 81 from 74 balls, and Neil Fairbrother had hammered 128 from 18 overs to take Lancashire to 262 for seven at Derby.
Rain reduced Derbyshire's target to 252 from 38 overs but they managed only 217 for nine.
